newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West spot power prices gain in late trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West spot power prices gain in late trade.

text.p: Spot power prices in the western U.S. moved higher in late trade following firmer spot natural gas prices, trade sources said Wednesday.
"The cold wave in the Midwest sucked a whole bunch of gas out of storage, and that is pushing up the cash market for gas in the West," said one trader.
"Things really sprang to life late today," he added.
With temperatures at normal or above-normal levels for most of the West since late last week, the power market has been lackluster.
But December San Juan natural gas prices moved a few cents higher Wednesday to $2.36-$2.37 per million British thermal units, equivalent to another 40 cents per megawatt hour (MWh) of electricity.
First-quarter 1997 Palo Verde was said to trade at $17.50 per MWh early Wednesday and at $18.20 later in the day.
Cash December Palo Verde was quoted $21.50-22.00 in late trade, compared with $21.15-21.40 earlier in the day.
Utility sources in the West emphasized that regional gas storage is near target levels, but diversion of spot supplies to the East and Midwest has pushed spot prices higher.
"The Alberta (gas) contract on NYMEX was way up today," noted one trader.
NYMEX December Alberta natgas closed 18 cents higher at $1.51 after setting a new contract high of $1.55.
